I noticed unexpectedly large air resistance in the Panda model and traced it to the fingertip inertial parameters.

In [[panda_gripper.xml](https://github.com/ARISE-Initiative/robosuite/blob/v1.5.1/robosuite/models/assets/grippers/panda_gripper.xml#L33-L44)](https://github.com/ARISE-Initiative/robosuite/blob/v1.5.1/robosuite/models/assets/grippers/panda_gripper.xml#L33-L44), both fingertip bodies have:

```xml
mass="0.01" diaginertia="0.01 0.01 0.01"
```

For a 10 g fingertip, these inertia values seem much too large. They also affect air resistance: MuJoCo’s default [[inertia-based fluid model](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.3.5/computation/fluid.html#inertia-model)](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.3.5/computation/fluid.html#inertia-model) derives an equivalent box from each body’s mass and inertia. These values produce a box approximately **2.45 m on each side** for each fingertip.

Since robosuite’s [[base.xml](https://github.com/ARISE-Initiative/robosuite/blob/v1.5.1/robosuite/models/assets/base.xml#L4)](https://github.com/ARISE-Initiative/robosuite/blob/v1.5.1/robosuite/models/assets/base.xml#L4) enables air density and viscosity by default, this leads to substantial drag even at moderate joint velocities.

### Reproduction

Tested with robosuite 1.5.1, MuJoCo 3.3.5 and Python 3.10. The corresponding XML parameters are also unchanged in v1.5.2.

The following uses the stock Panda Lift environment without rendering or custom patches. It sets only joint 7’s velocity to 0.9 rad/s, then compares passive joint forces with and without fluid forces at the same state. No simulation steps or controller updates are performed.

```python
import numpy as np
import mujoco
import robosuite as suite

env = suite.make(
    "Lift",
    robots="Panda",
    initialization_noise=None,
    has_renderer=False,
    has_offscreen_renderer=False,
    use_camera_obs=False,
)

try:
    env.reset()
    m, d = env.sim.model._model, env.sim.data._data
    dofs = np.asarray(env.robots[0]._ref_joint_vel_indexes)

    d.qvel[:] = 0
    d.qvel[dofs[6]] = 0.9
    air = (m.opt.density, m.opt.viscosity)

    def passive(density, viscosity):
        m.opt.density, m.opt.viscosity = density, viscosity
        mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
        return d.qfrc_passive[dofs].copy()

    fluid_torque = passive(*air) - passive(0, 0)
    print("density, viscosity:", air)
    print("fluid torque [J1..J7], Nm:", np.round(fluid_torque, 6))
finally:
    env.close()
```

Output:

```text
density, viscosity: (1.2, 2e-05)
fluid torque [J1..J7], Nm: [ 5.430331  0.        5.190448  0.       -5.365467  0.       -5.474594]
```

This gives approximately **5.47 N·m of opposing fluid torque at joint 7**, with only 0.9 rad/s of joint velocity.

As a diagnostic, I also changed only the two fingertip inertia diagonals to `1e-6`, leaving their masses and the air settings unchanged. The magnitude of joint 7’s fluid torque dropped to approximately **0.116 N·m**. That value is not intended as a proposed physical calibration; it just helps isolate the contribution of the fingertip inertias.

Are the current fingertip inertia values intentional, perhaps for numerical stability? If not, could they be replaced with values consistent with the fingertip mass and geometry? Disabling density and viscosity avoids the drag, but does not correct the inertias themselves.

One other Panda parameter I noticed while checking this: [[robot.xml](https://github.com/ARISE-Initiative/robosuite/blob/v1.5.1/robosuite/models/assets/robots/panda/robot.xml#L4-L12)](https://github.com/ARISE-Initiative/robosuite/blob/v1.5.1/robosuite/models/assets/robots/panda/robot.xml#L4-L12) sets joint 5’s torque limit to ±80 N·m, whereas the [[Franka Panda/FER specification](https://frankarobotics.github.io/docs/robot_specifications.html#limits-for-franka-emika-robot-fer)](https://frankarobotics.github.io/docs/robot_specifications.html#limits-for-franka-emika-robot-fer) lists ±12 N·m. Is that also an intentional simulation setting, or an oversight?

### Bug Description

`UsdPhysics.DriveAPI` defines the stiffness and damping of an angular drive per degree ([UsdPhysicsDriveAPI reference](https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_physics_drive_a_p_i.html), [schema.usda](https://github.com/PixarAnimationStudios/OpenUSD/blob/96c1989167d2aaab5bd34627f32a321a6b79866b/pxr/usd/usdPhysics/schema.usda#L857-L873)):

> Stiffness of the drive. Units: if linear drive: mass/second/second if angular drive: mass\*DIST_UNITS\*DIST_UNITS/degrees/second/second.
>
> Damping of the drive. Units: if linear drive: mass/second If angular drive: mass\*DIST_UNITS\*DIST_UNITS/second/degrees.

The USD parser copies both values into `dofs_kp` / `dofs_kv` unchanged for every joint type ([usd_rigid_entity.py#L446-L447](https://github.com/Genesis-Embodied-AI/genesis-world/blob/439a26f56097c4178fbabf6a45f9d01662288be3/genesis/utils/usd/usd_rigid_entity.py#L446-L447)), while joint positions are radians. So every revolute drive, and every `rotX` / `rotY` / `rotZ` drive of a spherical joint, gets 180/pi = 57.3x too little stiffness and damping: its natural frequency and damping ratio are both sqrt(57.3) = 7.6x too low. The same function already converts joint limits from degrees ([L326-L327](https://github.com/Genesis-Embodied-AI/genesis-world/blob/439a26f56097c4178fbabf6a45f9d01662288be3/genesis/utils/usd/usd_rigid_entity.py#L326-L327)). Linear drive gains are per meter and are fine.

Other USD consumers apply the conversion: Newton's importer ([_resolution_policy.py#L291-L300](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/98ec5897436215f8274903a6757e109e2f920f63/newton/_src/usd/_resolution_policy.py#L291-L300)), Isaac Lab when it writes drives ([schemas.py#L1502-L1510](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/1279faaa700e0926a4a7cd0da2d61df6551ed07a/source/isaaclab/isaaclab/sim/schemas/schemas.py#L1502-L1510)), and Isaac Sim's articulation gains ([articulation.py#L2543-L2553](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacSim/blob/9160c0e95d85da98cb3906402f5784b6ad2bc33f/source/deprecated/isaacsim.core.prims/python/impl/articulation.py#L2543-L2553)).

`test_joints_mjcf_vs_usd` passes today because its USD fixture puts the MJCF actuator's per-radian gains (kp 120, kv 12) unchanged on the angular drive ([conftest.py#L1316-L1318](https://github.com/Genesis-Embodied-AI/genesis-world/blob/439a26f56097c4178fbabf6a45f9d01662288be3/tests/parsers/conftest.py#L1316-L1318)), which the schema reads as 120 N\*m/deg.

Genesis's own USD test assets follow the schema: the UR10 in the `Genesis-Intelligence/assets` dataset authors stiffness 349.0659 (= 20000 \* pi/180) and damping 34.9066 (= 2000 \* pi/180) on all six joints. Main reads kp 349.07 and kv 34.91; with the fix below, 20000 and 2000. The Humanoid's gains come out as round numbers too (kp 2, 5, 10, 20; kv 0.1, 1, 5).

### Steps to Reproduce

The script writes a stage with one revolute joint (inertia 0.1 kg\*m^2 about a vertical axis through the link's center of mass, so gravity exerts no torque about it) and an angular drive with stiffness 1 N\*m/deg and damping 0.01 N\*m\*s/deg. It imports the stage on the CPU backend, prints the parsed gains, then measures the free response around the drive target (dt 1 ms, 7000 steps, 5 deg initial deflection) and compares it with the analytic one.

<details><summary>repro_usd_angular_drive_units.py</summary>

```python
"""Genesis reads UsdPhysics angular drive gains per radian, but the schema authors them per degree.

The script writes a USD stage with one revolute joint driven by a UsdPhysics.DriveAPI("angular") of stiffness K and
damping D, imports it with Genesis on CPU, then compares
  (a) the actuator gains Genesis parsed with the authored ones converted to per radian, and
  (b) the simulated free response around the drive target with the analytic one.

UsdPhysics.DriveAPI units (https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_physics_drive_a_p_i.html):
  stiffness, angular drive: mass*DIST_UNITS*DIST_UNITS/degrees/second/second, i.e. N*m/deg
  damping, angular drive:   mass*DIST_UNITS*DIST_UNITS/second/degrees, i.e. N*m*s/deg
Joint positions in Genesis are radians, so the spec gives kp = K * 180/pi and kv = D * 180/pi.
"""

import math
import os
import tempfile

import numpy as np
from pxr import Gf, Usd, UsdGeom, UsdPhysics

import genesis as gs

K_DEG = 1.0  # authored angular drive stiffness [N*m/deg]
D_DEG = 0.01  # authored angular drive damping [N*m*s/deg]
I_AXIS = 0.1  # link inertia about the hinge axis, which passes through the link center of mass [kg*m^2]
Q0_DEG = 5.0  # initial deflection from the drive target (0 deg)
DT, N_STEPS = 1e-3, 7000  # fixed time step [s] and number of steps (7 s)


def write_stage(path):
    stage = Usd.Stage.CreateNew(path)
    UsdGeom.SetStageUpAxis(stage, UsdGeom.Tokens.z)
    UsdGeom.SetStageMetersPerUnit(stage, 1.0)
    UsdPhysics.SetStageKilogramsPerUnit(stage, 1.0)
    root = UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/robot")
    stage.SetDefaultPrim(root.GetPrim())

    # Static base: a collider without RigidBodyAPI.
    base = UsdGeom.Cube.Define(stage, "/robot/base")
    base.GetSizeAttr().Set(0.2)
    UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI.Apply(base.GetPrim())
    UsdPhysics.ArticulationRootAPI.Apply(base.GetPrim())

    # Moving link 1 m away from the base, with an authored mass and inertia.
    link = UsdGeom.Cube.Define(stage, "/robot/link")
    link.AddTranslateOp().Set(Gf.Vec3d(1.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    link.GetSizeAttr().Set(0.2)
    UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI.Apply(link.GetPrim())
    mass_api = UsdPhysics.MassAPI.Apply(link.GetPrim())
    mass_api.CreateMassAttr(1.0)
    mass_api.CreateCenterOfMassAttr(Gf.Vec3f(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    mass_api.CreateDiagonalInertiaAttr(Gf.Vec3f(I_AXIS, I_AXIS, I_AXIS))
    mass_api.CreatePrincipalAxesAttr(Gf.Quatf(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0))

    # Vertical hinge through the link center of mass, so gravity exerts no torque about it.
    hinge = UsdPhysics.RevoluteJoint.Define(stage, "/robot/hinge")
    hinge.CreateBody0Rel().SetTargets([base.GetPath()])
    hinge.CreateBody1Rel().SetTargets([link.GetPath()])
    hinge.CreateAxisAttr(UsdPhysics.Tokens.z)
    hinge.CreateLocalPos0Attr(Gf.Vec3f(1.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    hinge.CreateLocalPos1Attr(Gf.Vec3f(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    drive = UsdPhysics.DriveAPI.Apply(hinge.GetPrim(), "angular")
    drive.CreateTypeAttr("force")
    drive.CreateStiffnessAttr(K_DEG)
    drive.CreateDampingAttr(D_DEG)
    drive.CreateTargetPositionAttr(0.0)
    stage.Save()


def measure(qs, dt):
    """Natural frequency and damping ratio of a free response from its positive peaks (log decrement)."""
    i_pk = np.flatnonzero((qs[1:-1] > qs[:-2]) & (qs[1:-1] >= qs[2:]) & (qs[1:-1] > 1e-3 * np.max(qs))) + 1
    # Refine each peak with the parabola through its three samples.
    y0, y1, y2 = qs[i_pk - 1], qs[i_pk], qs[i_pk + 1]
    shift = 0.5 * (y0 - y2) / (y0 - 2.0 * y1 + y2)
    t_pk = (i_pk + 1 + shift) * dt
    a_pk = y1 - 0.25 * (y0 - y2) * shift
    period = np.mean(np.diff(t_pk))
    delta = math.log(a_pk[0] / a_pk[-1]) / (len(a_pk) - 1)
    zeta = delta / math.sqrt(4.0 * math.pi**2 + delta**2)
    omega_n = 2.0 * math.pi / period / math.sqrt(1.0 - zeta**2)
    return omega_n, zeta, len(a_pk)


def main():
    gs.init(backend=gs.cpu, precision="64", seed=0, logging_level="warning")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        path = os.path.join(tmp_dir, "hinge.usda")
        write_stage(path)
        scene = gs.Scene(
            sim_options=gs.options.SimOptions(dt=DT, gravity=(0.0, 0.0, -9.81)),
            rigid_options=gs.options.RigidOptions(enable_collision=False),
            show_viewer=False,
        )
        # default_armature=None keeps the link inertia as the only inertia about the hinge.
        robot = scene.add_entity(gs.morphs.USD(file=path, default_armature=None))
        scene.build()

    dofs_idx = robot.get_joint("/robot/hinge").dofs_idx_local
    kp = float(robot.get_dofs_kp(dofs_idx)[0])
    kv = float(robot.get_dofs_kv(dofs_idx)[0])
    armature = float(robot.get_dofs_armature(dofs_idx)[0])
    inertia = I_AXIS + armature

    # Free response around the drive target. The importer leaves targetPosition unread, so the script commands the
    # same target (0) through the API.
    robot.set_dofs_position([math.radians(Q0_DEG)], dofs_idx)
    robot.control_dofs_position([0.0], dofs_idx)
    qs = np.empty(N_STEPS)
    for i in range(N_STEPS):
        scene.step()
        qs[i] = float(robot.get_dofs_position(dofs_idx)[0])
    omega_meas, zeta_meas, n_peaks = measure(qs, DT)

    kp_spec, kv_spec = K_DEG * 180.0 / math.pi, D_DEG * 180.0 / math.pi
    omega_spec = math.sqrt(kp_spec / inertia)
    zeta_spec = kv_spec / (2.0 * math.sqrt(kp_spec * inertia))
    omega_raw = math.sqrt(K_DEG / inertia)
    zeta_raw = D_DEG / (2.0 * math.sqrt(K_DEG * inertia))

    print(f"genesis {gs.__file__}")
    print(f"authored: stiffness {K_DEG} N*m/deg, damping {D_DEG} N*m*s/deg; inertia about hinge {inertia} kg*m^2")
    print(f"dt {DT} s, {N_STEPS} steps, initial deflection {Q0_DEG} deg, {n_peaks} peaks used")
    print()
    print("(a) parsed gains (closer to 'spec' is better)")
    print(f"  {'':16}{'parsed':>12}{'spec':>12}{'raw (no conversion)':>22}{'parsed / spec':>15}")
    print(f"  {'kp [N*m/rad]':16}{kp:12.5f}{kp_spec:12.5f}{K_DEG:22.5f}{kp / kp_spec:15.5f}")
    print(f"  {'kv [N*m*s/rad]':16}{kv:12.5f}{kv_spec:12.5f}{D_DEG:22.5f}{kv / kv_spec:15.5f}")
    print()
    print("(b) simulated free response (closer to 'spec' is better)")
    print(f"  {'':22}{'measured':>12}{'spec':>12}{'raw (no conversion)':>22}{'spec / measured':>17}")
    print(f"  {'natural freq [rad/s]':22}{omega_meas:12.5f}{omega_spec:12.5f}{omega_raw:22.5f}{omega_spec / omega_meas:17.5f}")
    print(f"  {'damping ratio [-]':22}{zeta_meas:12.5f}{zeta_spec:12.5f}{zeta_raw:22.5f}{zeta_spec / zeta_meas:17.5f}")
    print()
    is_ok = abs(omega_meas / omega_spec - 1.0) < 0.01 and abs(zeta_meas / zeta_spec - 1.0) < 0.01
    print(f"matches UsdPhysics units within 1%: {'YES' if is_ok else 'NO'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

Output on main (439a26f):

```
authored: stiffness 1.0 N*m/deg, damping 0.01 N*m*s/deg; inertia about hinge 0.1 kg*m^2
dt 0.001 s, 7000 steps, initial deflection 5.0 deg, 3 peaks used
(a) parsed gains (closer to 'spec' is better)
                        parsed        spec   raw (no conversion)  parsed / spec
  kp [N*m/rad]         1.00000    57.29578               1.00000        0.01745
  kv [N*m*s/rad]       0.01000     0.57296               0.01000        0.01745
(b) simulated free response (closer to 'spec' is better)
                            measured        spec   raw (no conversion)  spec / measured
  natural freq [rad/s]       3.16220    23.93654               3.16228          7.56958
  damping ratio [-]          0.01581     0.11968               0.01581          7.56959
matches UsdPhysics units within 1%: NO
```

The simulation itself is right: it matches the analytic response of the unconverted gains (3.16228 rad/s, 0.01581). Spherical joints behave the same: `rotX` / `rotY` / `rotZ` drives of stiffness 1, 2, 3 N\*m/deg come out as kp 1, 2, 3 instead of 57.3, 114.6, 171.9.

### Expected Behavior

kp = stiffness \* 180/pi and kv = damping \* 180/pi for angular drives, linear drives unchanged. With the change below, the same script prints:

```
  kp [N*m/rad]        57.29578    57.29578               1.00000        1.00000
  kv [N*m*s/rad]       0.57296     0.57296               0.01000        1.00000
  natural freq [rad/s]      23.90293    23.93654               3.16228          1.00141
  damping ratio [-]          0.11951     0.11968               0.01581          1.00145
matches UsdPhysics units within 1%: YES
```

The 0.14% left is time discretization: it drops to 0.04% at dt = 0.25 ms.

### Environment

- OS: Linux x86_64 (CentOS Stream 10)
- GPU/CPU: CPU backend (x86_64), no GPU
- GPU-driver version: N/A
- CUDA / CUDA-toolkit version: N/A
- Python 3.12.15, torch 2.15.0+cpu, usd-core 26.11, quadrants 1.4.0

### Release version or Commit ID

main, 439a26f56097c4178fbabf6a45f9d01662288be3. The same lines are in v1.3.0, v1.4.0, v1.4.5, v1.4.6 and v1.4.7.

### Additional Context

Proposed fix:

```diff
@@ -455,6 +455,9 @@ def _parse_link(
             kp = np.asarray(dofs_kp, dtype=gs.np_float)
             kv = np.asarray(dofs_kv, dtype=gs.np_float)
+            if joint_type in (gs.JOINT_TYPE.REVOLUTE, gs.JOINT_TYPE.SPHERICAL):
+                # UsdPhysics gives angular drive stiffness and damping per degree, while joint positions are radians.
+                kp, kv = np.rad2deg(kp), np.rad2deg(kv)
             j_info["dofs_act_gain"] = kp
```

The `all_joints_usd` fixture then authors the MJCF gains in the schema's units, `np.deg2rad(120.0)` and `np.deg2rad(12.0)` (120 N\*m/rad is 2.094 N\*m/deg). `test_joints_mjcf_vs_usd` fails on main with it (USD kp 2.094 vs MJCF 120) and passes with the fix. All of `tests/parsers/test_usd.py` passes with the fix (33 passed, 2 skipped without omniverse-kit), as it does on main.

### Intro

Hi!

I work on [mujoco-usd-converter](https://github.com/newton-physics/mujoco-usd-converter), which converts MJCF to OpenUSD with the MjcPhysics schemas, and I check its output with MuJoCo's USD decoder.

### My setup

MuJoCo 4.0.1 with `mujoco-usd` 4.0.1 from PyPI (`usd-core` 25.11), Python 3.12, Linux x86_64. The same code is in 3.17.0 and on `main`.

### What's happening? What did you expect?

The decoder applies `mjc:compiler:inertiaGroupRange:min` and `mjc:compiler:inertiaGroupRange:max` only when both have an authored value. If only one is authored, it warns and ignores both:

```
WARNING: Only one of inertiaGroupRangeMin and inertiaGroupRangeMax was authored, ignoring both.
```

An unauthored attribute resolves to its schema fallback, which for these attributes is MuJoCo's default (`min = 0`, `max = 5`). So a stage that authors only `max = 1` describes `inertiagrouprange="0 1"`, but it decodes as `0 5`. That is the natural way to author a range that keeps one default end, such as `"0 1"` or `"0 3"`, since authoring tools commonly skip values that match the schema fallback. Geoms in groups MuJoCo should exclude from inertia then contribute mass.

I expected the decoder to use the resolved value of each attribute, taking the schema fallback for whichever end is not authored. The other `MjcSceneAPI` compiler attributes are applied independently whenever each one is authored.

The check is in [`usd_decoder.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/4.0.1/plugin/usd_decoder/usd_decoder.cc#L866-L883).

### Steps for reproduction

1. `pip install mujoco-usd==4.0.1`
2. Run the code below. It builds the same stage twice, with only `max` authored and with both ends authored. The body has a 0.2 m box in group 0 (8 kg) and a 0.3 m radius sphere collider in group 2, which is outside the range.
3. With only `max` authored, the range decodes as `[0, 5]` and the body mass is 121.10 kg. Authoring the default `min = 0` as well gives the expected `[0, 1]` and 8.00 kg.

```
WARNING: Only one of inertiaGroupRangeMin and inertiaGroupRangeMax was authored, ignoring both.
min authored=False: inertiagrouprange=[0, 5] body mass=121.10
min authored=True: inertiagrouprange=[0, 1] body mass=8.00
```

### Minimal model for reproduction

The stage is built in memory by the code below. The equivalent MJCF, which compiles to 8 kg:

<details>
<summary>minimal XML</summary>

```XML
<mujoco>
  <compiler inertiagrouprange="0 1"/>
  <worldbody>
    <body>
      <freejoint/>
      <geom type="box" size="0.1 0.1 0.1" group="0"/>
      <geom type="sphere" size="0.3" group="2"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
```
</details>

### Code required for reproduction

```python
import mujoco
from pxr import Usd, UsdGeom, UsdPhysics


def make_stage(author_min: bool) -> Usd.Stage:
    stage = Usd.Stage.CreateInMemory()
    UsdGeom.SetStageMetersPerUnit(stage, 1.0)
    UsdGeom.SetStageUpAxis(stage, UsdGeom.Tokens.z)

    scene = UsdPhysics.Scene.Define(stage, "/PhysicsScene").GetPrim()
    scene.ApplyAPI("MjcSceneAPI")
    # Equivalent to <compiler inertiagrouprange="0 1"/>. The min of 0 is the schema default.
    scene.GetAttribute("mjc:compiler:inertiaGroupRange:max").Set(1)
    if author_min:
        scene.GetAttribute("mjc:compiler:inertiaGroupRange:min").Set(0)

    body = UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/World/body").GetPrim()
    UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI.Apply(body)

    # 0.2 m box in group 0: 8 kg at the default density of 1000.
    box = UsdGeom.Cube.Define(stage, "/World/body/box")
    box.GetSizeAttr().Set(0.2)
    UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI.Apply(box.GetPrim())

    # 0.3 m radius sphere in group 2, outside the range, so it should not contribute mass.
    sphere = UsdGeom.Sphere.Define(stage, "/World/body/sphere")
    sphere.GetRadiusAttr().Set(0.3)
    UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI.Apply(sphere.GetPrim())
    sphere.GetPrim().ApplyAPI("MjcCollisionAPI")
    sphere.GetPrim().GetAttribute("mjc:group").Set(2)
    return stage


for author_min in (False, True):
    stage = make_stage(author_min)
    spec = mujoco.MjSpec.from_file(stage.GetRootLayer().identifier)
```

### Description

Deleting an articulation and spawning it again breaks the Fabric world transforms of its link meshes, but only on the first respawn. `omni.rtx` logs five `CUDA error in memcpy: invalid argument` errors during `sim.reset()`, and the plain (only for non-instanced) Mesh children of the articulation links are rendered with zero `omni:fabric:worldMatrix`. Every later delete/respawn of the same asset is clean, so currently we literally have to `reset()` the simulation multiple times before we can simulate such articulations.

Below you can find a (LLM-generated, but nevertheless functional) script that reproduces the problem. Some observations:

- Cycle 1 (first spawn) is clean, cycle 2 (first respawn) breaks, cycles 3 and later are clean.
- It is not once per process. A different articulated asset that is spawned later breaks again on its own first respawn. A byte-identical copy of the USD file breaks too, so it is not tied to the file.
- Keeping a second copy of the same articulation alive for the whole run (`--keeper`) prevents it.
- Putting each link's meshes in an instanceable prim (`--instanced`) prevents it.
- Without an RTX camera (`--cameras 0`) it does not happen.
- Spawning the new copy at another path before deleting the old one does not prevent it.
- The world matrices are still correct right after `sim.reset()`. They turn to zero in the first `sim.step(render=True)`. More fine-grained debugging is not possible because the code is closed-source.
- The same happens with a real-world asset (a cabinet with prismatic drawers taken from LIBERO).
- Rarely (about 1 in 10 runs) the process aborts instead, in `libusdrt.hydra.fabric_scene_delegate.plugin.so`. I have no idea why.

Our guess is that Fabric frees the GPU columns of a bucket when its last prim is deleted, and that the first refill copies from the stale device pointer.

The error is logged synchronously on the main thread. Python stack at the first error:

```python
"""Deleting and respawning an articulation breaks the Fabric world transforms of its link meshes on the first respawn.

Each cycle stops the sim, deletes the articulation, spawns it again at the same prim path, calls sim.reset() and
renders two steps with one RTX camera. Then it checks every mesh under the articulation: its
omni:fabric:worldMatrix must equal omni:fabric:localMatrix x the parent's worldMatrix, and omni.rtx must not log
"CUDA error in memcpy".

The articulation is written by this script: three links (Xform + RigidBodyAPI) on a prismatic and a fixed joint, each
with three plain Mesh children.

    ./isaaclab.sh -p repro_articulation_respawn.py               # cycle 2 breaks
    ./isaaclab.sh -p repro_articulation_respawn.py --keeper      # a second copy stays alive: clean
    ./isaaclab.sh -p repro_articulation_respawn.py --instanced   # link meshes inside instanceable prims: clean
    ./isaaclab.sh -p repro_articulation_respawn.py --cameras 0   # no RTX camera: clean
"""

import argparse

from isaaclab.app import AppLauncher

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--cycles", type=int, default=4)
parser.add_argument("--cameras", type=int, default=1)
parser.add_argument("--keeper", action="store_true", help="Spawn a second copy once and never delete it.")
parser.add_argument("--instanced", action="store_true", help="Put each link's meshes in an instanceable prim.")
AppLauncher.add_app_launcher_args(parser)
args = parser.parse_args()
args.headless = True
args.enable_cameras = True
app = AppLauncher(args).app

import gc  # noqa: E402

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import omni.log  # noqa: E402
import omni.usd  # noqa: E402
import usdrt  # noqa: E402
from pxr import Gf, Sdf, Usd, UsdGeom, UsdPhysics  # noqa: E402

import isaaclab.sim as sim_utils  # noqa: E402
from isaaclab.actuators import ImplicitActuatorCfg  # noqa: E402
from isaaclab.assets import Articulation, ArticulationCfg  # noqa: E402
from isaaclab.sensors import Camera, CameraCfg  # noqa: E402

USD_PATH = "/tmp/repro_cabinet.usda"
ASSET_PATH = "/World/Cabinet"


def write_cabinet(path: str, instanced: bool) -> None:
    stage = Usd.Stage.CreateNew(path)
    UsdGeom.SetStageUpAxis(stage, UsdGeom.Tokens.z)
    root = UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/Cabinet").GetPrim()
    stage.SetDefaultPrim(root)
    UsdPhysics.ArticulationRootAPI.Apply(root)
    links = {"base": (0.0, 0.0, 0.2), "drawer": (0.05, 0.0, 0.25), "handle": (0.16, 0.0, 0.25)}
    sizes = {"base": (0.3, 0.3, 0.05), "drawer": (0.25, 0.25, 0.08), "handle": (0.02, 0.1, 0.02)}
    for name, position in links.items():
        link = UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, f"/Cabinet/{name}")
        link.AddTranslateOp().Set(Gf.Vec3d(*position))
        UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI.Apply(link.GetPrim())
        UsdPhysics.MassAPI.Apply(link.GetPrim()).CreateMassAttr(1.0)
        holder = f"/Cabinet/{name}"
        if instanced:
            holder = f"/Prototypes/{name}"
            UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, holder)
            visuals = UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, f"/Cabinet/{name}/visuals").GetPrim()
            visuals.GetReferences().AddInternalReference(Sdf.Path(holder))
            visuals.SetInstanceable(True)
        for i in range(3):
            mesh = UsdGeom.Mesh.Define(stage, f"{holder}/box_{i}")
            mesh.CreatePointsAttr([Gf.Vec3f(x, y, z) for x in (-0.5, 0.5) for y in (-0.5, 0.5) for z in (-0.5, 0.5)])
            mesh.CreateFaceVertexCountsAttr([4] * 6)
            mesh.CreateFaceVertexIndicesAttr([0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 7, 5, 0, 4, 5, 1, 2, 3, 7, 6, 0, 2, 6, 4, 1, 5, 7, 3])
            mesh.AddTranslateOp().Set(Gf.Vec3d(0.0, 0.0, 0.1 * (i - 1) if name == "base" else 0.0))
            mesh.AddScaleOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(*sizes[name]) * (1.0 - 0.03 * i))
            UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI.Apply(mesh.GetPrim())
            UsdPhysics.MeshCollisionAPI.Apply(mesh.GetPrim()).CreateApproximationAttr("convexHull")
    for joint_name, kind, body0, body1, local0 in (
        ("drawer_joint", UsdPhysics.PrismaticJoint, "base", "drawer", (0.05, 0.0, 0.05)),
        ("handle_joint", UsdPhysics.FixedJoint, "drawer", "handle", (0.11, 0.0, 0.0)),
    ):
        joint = kind.Define(stage, f"/Cabinet/{joint_name}")
        joint.CreateBody0Rel().SetTargets([Sdf.Path(f"/Cabinet/{body0}")])
        joint.CreateBody1Rel().SetTargets([Sdf.Path(f"/Cabinet/{body1}")])
        joint.CreateLocalPos0Attr(Gf.Vec3f(*local0))
        if kind is UsdPhysics.PrismaticJoint:
            joint.CreateAxisAttr("X")
            joint.CreateLowerLimitAttr(0.0)
            joint.CreateUpperLimitAttr(0.2)
    stage.Save()


def spawn(prim_path: str, y: float) -> Articulation:
    return Articulation(
        ArticulationCfg(
            prim_path=prim_path,
            spawn=sim_utils.UsdFileCfg(usd_path=USD_PATH),
            init_state=ArticulationCfg.InitialStateCfg(pos=(0.7, y, 0.05)),
            actuators={"all": ImplicitActuatorCfg(joint_names_expr=[".*"], stiffness=0.0, damping=10.0)},
        )
    )


def broken_prims() -> list[str]:
    """Prims under the articulation whose Fabric world matrix is not local x parent world."""

    def matrix(prim: object, name: str) -> np.ndarray | None:
        attr = prim.GetAttribute(name) if prim else None
        return np.array(attr.Get(), dtype=float).reshape(4, 4) if attr and attr.HasValue() else None

    fabric = usdrt.Usd.Stage.Attach(omni.usd.get_context().get_stage_id())
    broken = []
    for usd_prim in Usd.PrimRange(omni.usd.get_context().get_stage().GetPrimAtPath(ASSET_PATH)):
        prim = fabric.GetPrimAtPath(str(usd_prim.GetPath()))
        world, local = matrix(prim, "omni:fabric:worldMatrix"), matrix(prim, "omni:fabric:localMatrix")
        parent = matrix(fabric.GetPrimAtPath(str(usd_prim.GetParent().GetPath())), "omni:fabric:worldMatrix")
        if world is not None and local is not None and parent is not None:
            expected = local @ parent
            if np.abs(expected[3, :3] - world[3, :3]).max() > 0.01:
                broken.append(f"{usd_prim.GetPath()} world={world[3, :3].tolist()} expected={expected[3, :3].round(3).tolist()}")
    return broken


cuda_errors = 0


def count_cuda_errors(*log_args: object) -> None:
    global cuda_errors
    cuda_errors += any("CUDA error in memcpy" in str(a) for a in log_args)


log_consumer = omni.log.get_log().add_message_consumer(count_cuda_errors)

write_cabinet(USD_PATH, args.instanced)
sim = sim_utils.SimulationContext(sim_utils.SimulationCfg(dt=0.01))
sim_utils.DistantLightCfg(intensity=3000.0).func("/World/light", sim_utils.DistantLightCfg(intensity=3000.0))
sim_utils.GroundPlaneCfg().func("/World/ground", sim_utils.GroundPlaneCfg())
cameras = [
    Camera(
        CameraCfg(
            prim_path=f"/World/camera_{i}",
            height=180,
            width=320,
            data_types=["rgb"],
            spawn=sim_utils.PinholeCameraCfg(),
            offset=CameraCfg.OffsetCfg(pos=(-0.5, 0.2, 1.0), rot=(0.0, 0.3007, 0.0, 0.9537), convention="world"),
        )
    )
    for i in range(args.cameras)
]

keeper = spawn("/World/Keeper", y=-1.0) if args.keeper else None
cabinet = None
broken_cycles = []
for cycle in range(1, args.cycles + 1):
    cuda_errors = 0
    if cabinet is not None:
        sim.stop()
        sim_utils.delete_prim(ASSET_PATH)
        cabinet = None
        gc.collect()
    cabinet = spawn(ASSET_PATH, y=0.2)
    sim.reset()
    for _ in range(2):
        sim.step(render=True)
        for camera in cameras:
            camera.update(sim.get_physics_dt())
    broken = broken_prims()
    if broken or cuda_errors:
        broken_cycles.append(cycle)
    print(f"cycle {cycle}: broken_prims={len(broken)} cuda_memcpy_errors={cuda_errors}", flush=True)
    for entry in broken:
        print(f"    {entry}", flush=True)

print(f"RESULT: {'broken in cycles ' + str(broken_cycles) if broken_cycles else 'clean'}", flush=True)
app.close()
```

## Summary

On a small target with a 2 ms cycle, the introspection of `ros2_control` uses a large part of the realtime cycle. It causes cycle overruns at three moments:

1. In **every cycle**: `PUBLISH_ROS2_CONTROL_INTROSPECTION_DATA_ASYNC(DEFAULT_REGISTRY_KEY)` in `ControllerManager::update()` copies all registered values. With ~450 values (all state and command interfaces) this takes **~0.55–0.7 ms of each 2 ms cycle**.
2. In the **first cycle after the controller manager becomes INACTIVE**: the first publish of the new registry takes **~6.9 ms** (one cycle overrun at every start).
3. At **each activation or deactivation of a controller with introspection values**: `ControllerInterfaceBase` calls `enable_introspection(true/false)` in the lifecycle callbacks, which run in the realtime loop. The next `publishAsync()` handles the pending changes there. This pushed a cycle from below 2 ms to 2058–2245 µs.

Related: #3356 (publisher threads wake every cycle). This issue is about the cost **in the realtime thread**.

## Environment

- Bosch Rexroth ctrlX CORE X3 (arm64, 4 cores, 2 RT cores), ctrlX OS 4.6, real-time task with a 2 ms cycle.
- ROS 2 Jazzy, ros2_control fork based on Jazzy 4.x (same code on `master` for the parts below), pal_statistics 2.8.2.
- Hardware: UR10e (`ur_robot_driver`) + a mock gripper. The registry has 146 state interface values and 298 command interface values.

## Measurements

Times from the controller manager overrun warning, extended to print the parts of `update()` (fork PR https://github.com/b-robotized-forks/ros2_control/pull/32):

```
Overrun might occur, Total time : 2070.524 us (Expected < 2000.000 us)
  --> Read time : 36.531 us, Update time : 1998.152 us
      (Command limits time : 2.220 us, Introspection time : 694.855 us, Switch time : 1136.504 us)
```

`topic_stats.~/introspection_data.last_async_pub_duration` (time of `publishAsync()`, in the realtime thread) is ~0.55 ms in every cycle. About 500 publishes per second, with ~0.3 % `publish_async_failures`.

First cycle after `UNCONFIGURED -> INACTIVE` (no controllers loaded, command limits disabled, so only the introspection publish runs):

```
Overrun might occur, Total time : 6955.764 us (Expected < 2000.000 us)
  --> Read time : 35.161 us, Update time : 6891.553 us, Write time : 29.050 us
```

Controller with ~40 introspection values (`crisp_controllers/CartesianController` with `enable_introspection: true`), same switches with introspection on and off:

| | Activations / deactivations | Cycle overruns |
|---|---|---|
| introspection values registered in the ros2_control registry | 4 | 4 (2058–2245 µs) |
| no introspection values | 4 | 0 |
| values in an own `StatisticsRegistry` of the controller | 10 | 0 |

## Cause in the code

- `ControllerManager::update()` calls `PUBLISH_ROS2_CONTROL_INTROSPECTION_DATA_ASYNC` in every cycle. `RegistrationList::doUpdate()` copies all values.
- `ControllerInterfaceBase` calls `enable_introspection()` in `on_activate`/`on_deactivate`. That is `RegistrationsRAII::enableAll()`/`disableAll()`. The changes go to a lock-free queue. The next `publishAsync()` (realtime thread) runs `handlePendingDisables()` → `RegistrationList::setEnabled()` for each value. `setEnabled()` searches the id linearly in all registered values and calls `registrationsChanged()`. 40 values × ~490 entries.
- After the first `setEnabled(…, false)`, `all_enabled_` stays `false` (`all_enabled_ = all_enabled_ && enabled`). From then on `doUpdate()` always uses the slower path.

## Proposals

1. A parameter to publish the introspection data only every N cycles, or at a fixed rate, e.g. `introspection.publish_rate`.
2. A parameter to disable the introspection of state and/or command interfaces.
3. Do the first publish of a new registry outside the realtime loop. We do it in `on_configure` of the controller manager state machine, in the non-RT thread (fork PR #32). On the device this removed the start overrun (warm-up 7–11 ms in the non-RT thread).
4. Call `enable_introspection()` for controllers in the non-realtime part of the switch.
5. In pal_statistics: `setEnabled()` with an id-to-index map instead of a linear search, and compute `all_enabled_` again after an enable.

We can make PRs for these. Which of them do you want, and should 5 go to pal_statistics directly?

## Workaround in a controller

`crisp_controllers` now uses its own `pal_statistics::StatisticsRegistry` for its debug values. It does not register them in the ros2_control registry: https://github.com/learnsyslab/crisp_controllers/pull/79

If a Cartesian reference has no timing, the controller picks the timing itself so the end effector stays under `max_cartesian_speed` and `max_angular_speed`. With several waypoints the end effector can still move faster than these limits, by up to about 30%.

Why: each segment gets `1.5 * distance / max_speed` (`min_segment_duration()`). That factor is right for a single segment from rest to rest. But all waypoints are joined into one smooth spline (`fill_cubic_spline_velocities`), and then a segment can peak higher.

Example (translation only, `max_cartesian_speed = 0.1`, starting from rest):

| x waypoints [m] | synthesized segments [s] | peak speed [m/s] |
|---|---|---|
| 0 → 1 | 15 | 0.100 |
| 0 → 0.5 → 1 | 7.5, 7.5 | 0.100 |
| 0 → 1 → 0.9 | 15, 1.5 | 0.123 |
| 0 → 1 → 0.99 | 15, 0.15 | 0.128 |
| 0 → 1 → 0.999 | 15, 0.015 | 0.129 |

The overshoot happens when a long segment is followed by a short reversal. The angle channel uses the same factor, so `max_angular_speed` has the same problem.

Context: https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/pull/2664#discussion_r4308347761. Retiming against the solved spline's peaks would fix the speed but makes the spatial overshoot at the reversal worse. So it is left as a TODO in the code (`peak_speed_ratio`).

Possible directions:
- Retime iteratively until the solved spline's peaks are under the limit, and bound the overshoot separately.
- Use a velocity/acceleration-limited profile (e.g. trapezoidal or TOPP-style) instead of a fixed factor.
- Until then, document that the limits are approximate and only exact for single-segment moves.

Tests should cover multi-waypoint chunks with reversals.

new_candidates.body:
Follow-up to #2664 (refs #2435).

### What happens

The controller accepts and executes a trajectory even when the joint solution does not reach the commanded poses. Near singularities, at joint limits, for unreachable targets, or on chains with fewer than 6 DOF, the end effector drifts off the commanded line and no error is reported. A LIN move that does not stay on the line, without telling anyone, breaks the main promise of the controller.

The PR documents this under "Known limitations" in the userdoc. This issue tracks closing it.

### Why

`solve_ik_along_path` ([cartesian_trajectory_controller.cpp:287-345](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/blob/123d041e16dd8b069f996483b220085541c0842b/cartesian_trajectory_controller/src/cartesian_trajectory_controller.cpp#L287-L345)) samples the path every `resample_dt` and takes exactly one damped least-squares step per sample:

- `calculate_frame_difference(x_current, x_target)` -> `convert_cartesian_deltas_to_joint_deltas` -> `q += delta_q` (L321-332).
- The residual between FK(q) and the target is never computed. The only failure checks are plugin errors and `q.allFinite()`.
- The function always returns `true` at the end (L343: `TODO(vedh1234): reject the trajectory if IK does not converge`).
- Joint limits are not used (L331: `TODO(vedh1234): respect joint limits and resolve redundancy`). If the controller manager or the hardware clamps a joint, the executed tip pose differs from the planned one.

The KDL plugin computes `(J^T J + alpha I)^-1 J^T`. With `alpha > 0` this matrix is always invertible, so the step is always finite. That is the point of damping, but it also means the plugin never signals that a target is out of reach or that the Jacobian is singular. Only the caller can detect this, by checking the residual.

### Example

Toy model, not the controller: a 2-link planar arm (links 0.5 m, reach 1.0 m) using the same scheme with the controller defaults (`alpha = 0.01`, `resample_dt = 0.01`, 0.1 m/s). Position only, one DLS step per sample.

- Unreachable target: a straight line from (0.68, 0.47) to (1.30, 0.47), about 1.38 m from the base. The joint trajectory is finite. The final tip error is 607 mm, while the closest reachable point is only 381 mm away. Along the way the elbow flips (q2 goes from 1.2 to -1.37 rad).
- Joint limit: a reachable line that needs q2 up to about 2.4 rad. The IK error stays below 0.15 mm. If q2 is clamped to 2.0 rad at execution, the tip ends up 200 mm off the path.
- Near singularity: a line ending at 0.99 m reach. One step per sample gives 1.14 mm error. Five steps per sample give 0.12 mm.

On a real arm, this happens when a target lies just outside the workspace or when a wrist joint hits its limit. The message is accepted and the arm moves somewhere else.

### Proposed fix

1. After each sample, compute the residual between FK(q) and the target, both translation and rotation. Reject the message if it exceeds a new tolerance parameter, e.g. `ik.position_tolerance` / `ik.orientation_tolerance`. At minimum, check the final sample.
2. Allow a few Newton iterations per sample (parameter, default 1 to keep the current behaviour). Stop early once the error is within tolerance. This fixes most of the drift near singularities at little cost, since IK runs outside the RT loop.
3. Check every sample against the position limits (from `joint_limits` / URDF). Reject the message if one is exceeded. Clamping inside IK and then checking the residual is another option.
4. Optional: log or reject based on a singularity measure (e.g. smallest singular value of J, or manipulability). Damping hides this today.
5. Update the userdoc limitations once the checks are in.

### Tests

Current tests start from a well-conditioned home pose and only check paths that are reachable. None of them sends an unreachable or singular target or hits a joint limit.

- A target outside the workspace of the 6-DOF test robot: `build_joint_trajectory` returns false and the arm does not move.
- A path that needs a joint beyond its URDF limit: rejected.
- A path ending close to a singular configuration, inside tolerance: accepted, and the final tip error is below the tolerance.
- A 2-DOF chain with a target that needs orientation: rejected (or accepted only within tolerance, depending on how under-actuated chains are handled).

Related review discussion:
- Limitations listed in the userdoc on request: https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/pull/2664#discussion_r4308321635
- Joint limits left for later: https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/pull/2664#discussion_r4506130997

The new `cartesian_trajectory_controller` (#2664) requires the `joints` parameter to list the joints in kinematic chain order, from `kinematics.base` to `kinematics.tip`. Any other order fails configuration. The controller should accept any order instead, like `joint_trajectory_controller` does.

### Background

The kinematics plugin (KDL by default) takes joint vectors in URDF chain order and does not know the joint names. The controller passes vectors in `joints` order. If the two orders differ, FK and IK run on the wrong configuration. For now, `on_configure` rejects any order other than the chain order (review thread: https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/pull/2664#discussion_r4308347716).

JTC matches incoming trajectory joints by name. So the controller only needs one permutation between `joints` order and chain order.

### What to do

All in `cartesian_trajectory_controller/src/cartesian_trajectory_controller.cpp`:

1. In `on_configure`, keep `get_chain_joint_names()`. Replace the equality check (`params_.joints != chain_joints`) with a check that both lists hold the same joints. Then store the index of each chain joint in `params_.joints`.
2. In `build_joint_trajectory`, put the commanded positions (`q_seed`) and velocities (`start_velocity`) into chain order before using them.
3. In `solve_ik_along_path`, set `joint_traj.joint_names` to the chain order instead of `params_.joints`. JTC puts them back into its own order.
4. Keep the error when a chain joint is missing from `joints` or `joints` has extra joints.
5. Update the joint-order note in `doc/userdoc.rst`.

### Tests

In `test/test_cartesian_trajectory_controller.cpp`:

- Change `rejects_joints_not_in_chain_order` to configure with swapped joints and expect success.
- Check that the arm then tracks a straight line just as well as with the original order. `tracks_straight_line_with_rotation` shows how.
- Keep a test that rejects a missing or extra joint.

new_candidates.body:
`cartesian_trajectory_controller` (#2664) builds each joint trajectory from the state when the message arrives, but starts it at the message's `header.stamp`. These two times only match if the stamp is zero and IK takes no time. Otherwise the command jumps when the new trajectory takes over.

### Why

- The start state is the last commanded state, read when the message arrives (`rt_last_commanded_state_.get()` in `build_joint_trajectory`).
- That state becomes the first point of the joint trajectory, at `t=0` (`solve_ik_along_path`).
- `header.stamp` is copied to the joint trajectory unchanged, and JTC puts `t=0` at that stamp (`TODO(vedh1234): anchor at the stamped start, not at arrival`).

JTC's own handling of incoming messages avoids this. It only prepends the commanded state when the stamp is zero (`prepend_commanded_state`).

### Effect

With the default `allow_trajectory_replacement: true`:

| stamp | arm moving | effect |
|---|---|---|
| zero | yes | JTC keeps running the old trajectory while IK computes. The new first point is then a few ms old, so the arm gets a small backwards jump. |
| future | yes | The old trajectory runs until the stamp. Then the command jumps back to the state at arrival. This can be a large jump. |
| past | no, or replacement off | JTC starts partway into the new trajectory, so the command jumps forward. |

The userdoc lists the future-stamp case as a known limitation. The zero-stamp case was raised in review: https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/pull/2664#discussion_r4308347695

### Proposed fix

1. Pick the start time: the stamp if it is in the future, otherwise "now" plus a margin for the IK computation.
2. Take the start state by sampling JTC's active trajectory at that time, instead of the last commanded state. Use it as the IK seed, Cartesian waypoint 0 and start velocity.
3. Stamp the joint trajectory with that start time. Drop the explicit `t=0` point, so JTC's blending bridges from where the arm really is.
4. Remove the known limitation from the userdoc.

Sampling the active trajectory from the non-RT callback needs thread-safe access to it. Check how JTC exposes it at that point.

### Tests

- A chunk sent mid-motion with a zero stamp: commanded positions and velocities stay continuous at the handover.
- A chunk with a future stamp sent mid-motion: the old trajectory runs until the stamp, then the new one starts without a jump.
- A chunk with a past stamp from rest: no forward jump.

### Summary

With `general.buffer_backend: cuda` (5.6.0, ROS 2 Lyrical), the stereo node (`stereolabs::ZedCamera`) often publishes the **left image in the right image topic**. About half of the published stereo pairs have (nearly) identical eyes. The CPU path (`general.buffer_backend: cpu`) is correct. The mono node (`ZedCameraOne`) is not affected.

Downstream, stereo VSLAM breaks: zero disparity means infinite depth. With Isaac ROS cuVSLAM (stereo + IMU) on an 18 m loop, the final position error is 10–160 m with the CUDA transport and 0.04–0.2 m with CPU messages, from the same drive.

### Likely cause

`ZedCamera::initCudaBufferTransport()` initializes the transport with `retrieve_on_stream = true`:

```cpp
mCudaBuffer->init(mZed->getCUDAContext(), mZed->getCUDAStream(), true, err)
```

`getRetrieveStream()` then returns the transport's own non-blocking stream for every `retrieveImage(..., sl::MEM::GPU, ..., stream)`. That stream intentionally doesn't depend on the GPU work the SDK queues afterwards, and the grab thread calls the next `grab()` while the previous frame's retrieves may still be queued on it. Those retrieves can then run after the next grab has started overwriting the SDK's frame buffers.

`ZedCameraOne` initializes the same transport with `retrieve_on_stream = false` and isn't affected.

### Workaround (patch)

Retrieve on the default stream, synchronized with the SDK, as the mono node does:

```diff
--- a/zed_components/src/zed_camera/src/zed_camera_component_video_depth.cpp
+++ b/zed_components/src/zed_camera/src/zed_camera_component_video_depth.cpp
@@ initCudaBufferTransport()
-  // The data are retrieved on the transport stream (see `getRetrieveStream()`)
-  if (!mCudaBuffer->init(mZed->getCUDAContext(), mZed->getCUDAStream(), true, err)) {
+  if (!mCudaBuffer->init(mZed->getCUDAContext(), mZed->getCUDAStream(), false, err)) {
@@ getRetrieveStream()
-  if (gpu && mCudaBufferActive && mCudaBuffer) {
-    return mCudaBuffer->stream();
-  }
+  (void)gpu;
```

Publishing never overlaps a retrieve (`mVdMutex`), so the synchronous retrieve is enough. With this patch, all pairs are proper stereo pairs again, and cuVSLAM tracks with the CUDA transport: 0.14 m over 17.9 m, at twice the odometry rate of the CPU path.

### How we measured

The ZED X runs in simulation mode, receiving Isaac Sim 6.2's ZED X digital twin (zed-isaac-sim v5.4.0). ZED SDK 5.6.0, wrapper `1aa4249` (5.6.0), `rmw_fastrtps_cpp`, x86_64, RTX GPU.

For left/right gray (`~/left/gray/rect/image`, `~/right/gray/rect/image`) and colour, pairs are matched by stamp, and a pair counts as "alike" when the mean absolute difference is below 2 gray levels. The ground at about 2 m has a disparity of about 20 px, so a real pair differs by about 18 or more.

| transport | gray pairs alike | colour pairs alike |
|---|---|---|
| `cuda` | 22 / 50 (1 byte-identical) | 45 / 59 |
| `cpu` | 0 / 46 | 0 / 45 |
| `cuda` + patch above | 0 / 42 | 0 / 41 |

To rule out the transport, a subscriber received each image both as the CUDA buffer and as the CPU fallback. Bytes matched for every stamp, so the wrong content is already in the GPU buffer the node publishes.

We haven't tested it with a physical camera yet. Since the race is between the retrieves and the next `grab()`, it shouldn't be specific to the simulation input.
